slides.title: Procurement decision
bullets: Which candidates retain a credible rank when protonation assumptions change?
The protonation-state review changed the hit ranking.
Drelvessa Therapeutics SAS ordered the consensus-ranked compounds.
Docking prioritises experiments; it does not demonstrate activity.

slides.title: Data provenance
bullets: DT-6 virtual-library inputs are retained under {{PRJ0075:lims_id}}.
Engagement started 30 Sep 2013; interim readout 18 Oct 2013.
The final interpretation includes the protonation-state review completed for 06 Nov 2013.

slides.title: Virtual library triage
bullets: Reconcile parent identifiers before generating conformers.
Keep parent identity distinct from protonation and conformer variants.
Retain excluded entries and their disposition in the analysis notebook.

slides.title: Data acceptance
bullets: Check connectivity, stereochemical specification and duplicate parent entries.
Flag ambiguous ionisation assignments for explicit review.
Do not treat an unprepared entry as a poor docking result.

slides.title: Conformer preparation
bullets: Enumerate plausible conformers consistently across the candidate set.
Retain the preparation settings alongside the resulting variants.
Prevent a parent with many variants from gaining rank solely through more scoring opportunities.

slides.title: Initial docking interpretation
bullets: Compare candidates under a common preparation and scoring route.
Inspect poses as well as ordering.
Keep docking scores in kcal/mol; do not convert scores into predicted potency.

slides.title: Why protonation was revisited
bullets: Alternative protonation states change electrostatic interactions and pose plausibility.
A favourable score from a fragile assignment can mislead procurement.
The interim ordering therefore required a state-sensitivity review.

slides.title: State-sensitivity comparison
bullets: Associate each state-specific result with its parent identifier.
Compare relative ordering across plausible assignments.
Separate a stable candidate from a candidate favoured only by a particular assumption.

slides.title: Outcome of state review
bullets: The protonation-state review changed the hit ranking.
Use the reviewed ordering for procurement.
Retain the earlier ordering with its preparation assumptions so the change is traceable.

slides.title: Consensus ranking
bullets: Use agreement across plausible preparation choices as a robustness check.
Assess pose plausibility alongside score order.
Consensus is a selection aid, not a probability of binding.

slides.title: Hit clustering
bullets: Group related candidates to expose redundant procurement choices.
Keep chemical similarity separate from evidence of common activity.
Record the reasoning when a cluster representative is preferred.

slides.title: Procurement shortlist
bullets: The shortlist follows the consensus-ranked interpretation.
Drelvessa Therapeutics SAS ordered those compounds.
No individual structures, compound identifiers or numerical docking table are supplied in this readout pack.

slides.title: Model uncertainty
bullets: The scoring route approximates molecular interactions.
Alternative protonation assignments remain relevant at experimental conditions.
Procurement availability and sample identity require confirmation outside the docking model.

slides.title: Reproducibility handover
bullets: Dr E. Ostlund: preparation and docking interpretation.
Nadia Rahmani: parent-to-variant mapping and reproducibility records.
Dr T. Zawiernicki: engagement model gate.
Archive settings, ranking versions and procurement disposition under {{PRJ0075:lims_id}}.

slides.title: Next model gate
bullets: Test the procured candidates experimentally before claiming activity.
Return ambiguous or discordant observations to the preparation review.
Retain the consensus ranking as the rationale for selection.
Final readout | 06 Nov 2013 | Dr E. Ostlund
